answers.value: All production data pipelines orchestrated in the ITSM/scheduler with a business SLA tier (P1 finance/regulatory feeds, P2 analytics, P3 internal). Scope = the failed or late DAG run plus every downstream dependent job in the same lineage.
The current scheduling window for the affected run (e.g. nightly 02:00-06:00 ET batch load) up to the point the pipeline is confirmed recovered and caught up to the current watermark.

Incident record captures failed job id, run timestamp, error class (data/infra/dependency), SLA tier, root cause, and recovery action; all mandatory ITSM fields non-null before the ticket can be resolved.

Post-recovery row counts and control totals for the re-run match the source watermark within 0 variance for financial feeds and <=0.1% for analytics feeds; reconciliation query result attached to the incident.
Scheduler run log, error stack trace, and reconciliation output exported to the incident record with UTC timestamp and pipeline commit SHA; retained per the incident's 3-year audit retention.

Every SLA breach logged as an ITSM incident with disposition (recovered / re-run / data-quarantine / permanent-fail-escalated) and, if unresolved within the SLA tier, escalated to on-call SRE and the data product owner.
Runbook and recovery procedure for the pipeline are the latest approved version in Confluence, referenced by id in the incident; recovery steps executed match the approved runbook revision.
Alert thresholds: warn at 50% of SLA window elapsed with job still running, page on-call at 80%; late-data threshold = watermark lag > 30 min for P1, > 2 h for P2.
Any pipeline feeding a regulatory or GL filing is material; a missed P1 SLA or >0 reconciliation variance on a material feed triggers mandatory data product owner sign-off before close.
Sample of the last 20 SLA-breach incidents over the trailing quarter, weighted to include all P1 breaches.
Pass = pipeline recovered within its SLA tier (P1 <=2 h, P2 <=8 h, P3 next business day) and reconciliation clean; fail = SLA missed or reconciliation variance outside tolerance.

On persistent failure, quarantine partial output, open a P1 SDLC-Exception ticket owned by the Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day RCA SLA, and notify downstream data consumers via the ITSM broadcast.
Recovery executed against the runbook version tagged in the pipeline repo (git tag matching the deployed release), recorded in the incident.
Scheduler config and connection parameters sourced from the version-controlled IaC repo and the secrets vault; no manual parameter overrides permitted during recovery.

Acceptance = failed/late pipeline recovered within SLA tier, downstream jobs green, reconciliation clean; evidence = resolved ITSM incident with attached scheduler logs and reconciliation output at the incident record URL.

testing.value: Query incident history; P1 attainment >= 99% with all breaches ticketed.

answers.value: High-traffic and latency-sensitive components identified in the release scope (public APIs, quote/bind endpoints, batch ingestion). Scope = the specific service build/tag under test plus its direct downstream dependencies.
The performance test campaign for the current release candidate, run in the pre-production performance environment before the go/no-go gate.
Every scenario records p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (req/s), error rate, and resource utilisation; all fields populated in the test report before results are accepted.
Requests issued vs. responses recorded reconcile within 0.1%; unaccounted requests investigated and explained before the run is deemed valid.
Test plan, load profile, raw result files, and dashboards exported to the CI artifact store tagged with the build SHA and UTC run timestamp; retained for the release's audit window.
Any scenario breaching a target logged as a defect in Jira with severity, owner, and disposition (fix / accept-with-waiver / block-release).
Current-release p95 latency and throughput compared against the prior release baseline; no more than 5% latency regression permitted, and any regression waived requires Tech Lead sign-off.
Performance run linked to the release change ticket (Jira release id / change record) and to the CI pipeline run that produced the tested build.
The full set of performance scenarios for the release: steady-state load, peak (2x expected), soak (2 h), and spike; each executed against the tagged build.
Pass = p95 <= 500 ms, p99 <= 1 s, error rate < 0.1% at target throughput, and no > 5% regression vs. baseline; fail = any target breached.

On failure, block the release gate and open a Jira defect (type Performance) owned by the Tech Lead; a waiver requires an SDLC-Exception ticket approved by the Engineering Manager with a remediation plan and 10-business-day SLA.
Effective for the current release candidate; results expire and must be re-run if the build SHA changes before deployment.
Acceptance = all scenarios meet latency/throughput/error targets with no > 5% regression; evidence = signed performance report and dashboards in the CI artifact store keyed to the build SHA.

checklist.value: Performance suite executed against the release candidate in the pre-prod perf environment and gated in CI.

testing.value: Force a scenario over threshold; confirm the release pipeline stage fails and the gate blocks promotion.

On failure, block promotion and open a Jira defect owned by the Tech Lead; waiver via SDLC-Exception ticket approved by Engineering Manager with a 10-business-day remediation SLA.
